result.title: BrainBind: Bridging Synchronized EEG and fMRI through Long-Form Naturalistic Video Representations
result.comment: Accepted at BMVC 2026. 26 pages, 4 figures, including supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/Forainest789/Brainbind
result.summary: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. Most neural decoding systems, however, align one modality in isolation and mostly against static images or short clips. We study the synchronized case: EEG and fMRI are recorded during the same long-form naturalistic viewing, giving a shared stimulus but also recurring narrative context and many semantically similar candidates. We present BrainBind, a framework that maps synchronized EEG and fMRI into frozen long-form video embedding spaces and treats those spaces as common visual-semantic references, not literal neural codes. On CineBrain, a five-seed Recall@K 2 x 4 matrix across two video anchors and four system configurations shows distinct retrieval profiles. With Omni, fMRI organizes the full candidate list most strongly (MRR = 23.82, nDCG@10 = 25.31), while Joint-Dual gives the highest mean label-aware R@1 (13.52%) with a distinct rank-wide profile. The complementary episode-disjoint evaluation quantifies the contribution of repeated stimulus identity and narrative context to the random split. Across these experiments, proxy choice and system configuration produce distinct top-rank and rank-wide retrieval profiles within the present synchronized dataset. The code is available at https://github.com/Forainest789/Brainbind.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 BrainBind，将同步采集的 EEG 与 fMRI 映射到冻结的长视频嵌入空间，在 CineBrain 数据集上做跨模态检索，并比较不同代理空间与系统配置的检索表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 属脑信号解码与跨模态检索研究，不涉及模型内部推理状态、视觉证据使用或 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等决策过程；其检索评估与 episode-disjoint 划分虽涉及语义相近候选和情境混淆，但与 LVR 的表示形成和生成机制缺少可迁移的具体线索。
